subject: music
title: Motivic Development
welcome_lead: Take a tiny idea — extend, invert, augment, fragment.

concepts.def: Repetition of a motif at a different pitch.
Breaking a motif into smaller cells.

walkthroughs.body_html: A motif is the smallest recognisable idea — Beethoven's four-note opening to Symphony No. 5 (1808) is the textbook example. A theme is a longer melody, often built from motifs.
Apply each technique to your own motif during the compositional process. Examiners reward clear evidence of development, not just statement of ideas.

mcqs.q: Reversing the order of pitches is:
How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
All notes are raised by a semitone.

mcqs.q: What does 'piano' (p) mean as a dynamic marking?
What happens in the recapitulation of sonata form?
options: Both subjects return, but the second subject is now in the tonic key.

sequence.term: Choose the brief or free idea
sequence.def: Composing starts by fixing what the piece must do
Jot riffs, motifs and progressions before developing anything
Grow the strongest material into full musical sections
Decide the overall form once the sections exist
Notate and record the finished piece
Last of all: submit score/recording plus the required log
